extracted.intended_audience: Readers, commenters, event attendees, speakers, sponsors and volunteers of The Texas Tribune (Texas Tribune community members)
extracted.subtask_description: Official community guidelines and code of conduct for participating in The Texas Tribune’s online comment sections, events, and community groups, including rules, prohibited content, moderation procedures, and safety/reporting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: First-hand experiences, credible information and informed questions help build a constructive dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal arguments and attacks do not. Provide firsthand information or informed questions rather than attacks; aim to build constructive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: Debate ideas, not people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether you agree or disagree with another comment, follow the golden rule when addressing others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your comments relevant to the story or topic at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally read the story before commenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag bad behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the flag/report tool to mark questionable comments for moderator review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators will review flagged content. For urgent concerns email abuse@texastribune.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t be abusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Racist, sexist or otherwise bigoted comments; ad hominem attacks; and threatening language of any kind are strictly prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such content is disallowed under the Tribune’s commenting rules and may be removed under the terms of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t be a bully
rubrics_metrics.description: Commandeering a comment thread, dominating a conversation or other intimidating or disruptive behavior is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dominating discussions or using intimidation tactics; moderators may intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t be misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not post false or misleading information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you reference another source, cite it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t be spammy
rubrics_metrics.description: No fundraising, advertising, marketing or self-promotional material allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electioneering is also prohibited. Discussion of issues and ideas is encouraged; campaign or candidate stumping is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t violate someone’s privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not post another individual’s email, phone or other personally identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect others’ personally identifying information; posting such information is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribune moderation and removal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: We reserve the right to remove any user or comment for any reason at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may remove content or accounts, and the Tribune enforces rules at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account registration required to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: A texastribune.org account is required to comment since the new system launched on March 27, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously registered users from before that date must create new accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment editing window
rubrics_metrics.description: You have up to 3 minutes after posting a comment to make changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit by clicking the “edit” link in the upper-right corner of the comment window within the 3-minute window.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to flag and moderator hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Click the “report” link on a specific comment to flag it; moderators are active Monday to Friday, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. CST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For urgent issues email abuse@texastribune.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignore/mute users
rubrics_metrics.description: You can mute comments from any user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hover on the user’s name and click “ignore user.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: When a post or user is reported, the Tribune will review the content in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may remove content/accounts. Refrain from reporting posts that do not break the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content under terms of service
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that is patently offensive and promotes racism, bigotry, hatred or physical harm; harasses or advocates harassment; exploits people sexually or violently; contains nudity, violence or offensive subject matter; contains links to adult websites; or solicits personal information from anyone under 18, among other things, is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the full terms of service for a more detailed list of prohibited content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise consideration and respect at events
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring questions and a willingness to participate in respectful conversations; keep conversations professional and consider other parties’ points of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passionate conversations are expected, but do not make it personal and be mindful of boundaries of taste, humor, personal space and physical interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply when asked to stop harassing behavior at events
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants asked to stop any harassing behavior are expected to comply immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may result in expulsion and/or banning from future events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of harassing or inappropriate behavior at events
rubrics_metrics.description: Harassment and inappropriate behavior may include, but are not limited to: sexist, racist, homophobic, transphobic or otherwise discriminatory jokes or language; physical intimidation, stalking or following; sustained disruption of talks or events; posting or displaying sexually explicit or violent material; unwelcome sexual attention (including sexualized comments or jokes; inappropriate touching, groping and unwelcome sexual advances); advocating for or encouraging any of the above behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This non-exhaustive list illustrates behaviors that can lead to removal or further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited items at events
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not bring chairs, signs, anything that could be considered a weapon of any kind (gun, knife, large stick, projectiles, etc.), graffiti pens or spray paint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals bringing these items may be ejected from the Festival and have credentials revoked without refund. The Tribune reserves the right to disallow any other items deemed inappropriate, dangerous, threatening or inconvenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: No political campaigning at events
rubrics_metrics.description: No political campaigning at Texas Tribune events or Festival venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political campaigning is disallowed at conference-related social events, off-site locations and related online communities and social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for violating event Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants violating the Code of Conduct may be expelled from any Texas Tribune event (including Festival) without a refund, and/or banned from future Texas Tribune events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions are at the discretion of Tribune staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data use and privacy for Texas Tribune accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune may share your information with third-party service providers (analytics, email) to provide an optimal user experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune does not rent, sell or share information with nonaffiliated companies for direct marketing unless you give permission. See the privacy policy for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to report problems at events
rubrics_metrics.description: Alert Tribune staff if you notice dangerous situations, someone in distress or violations of the Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For emergencies call 9-1-1. For non-urgent feedback email events@texastribune.org.
